$comment: Rule catalog — reproducibility. Standards 15, 16. The configuration that lets a result be obtained again. Three entries carry detectors, and all three detect cheap structural facts — unpinned dependencies, absent configuration, committed notebook state — which are real and are a long way short of establishing that a result reproduces.

rules.title: The experiment configuration is recorded in full
rules.description: Each experiment's configuration is recorded in enough detail to rerun it: code version, data version, hyperparameters, environment and dependency versions, and random seeds.
rules.rationale: Reproducibility is a property of the record, not of the code. Everything needed to obtain the result again either was written down at the time or is gone, and which of the two is the case is only discovered when someone tries.
rules.remediation: Adopt a configuration file or an experiment-tracking tool and record the full parameter set per run, including the data version and the seeds.
rules.evidenceExpected: A configuration artifact per experiment — params.yaml, a conf directory, or tracked runs — carrying code version, data version, hyperparameters, environment, and seeds.
rules.$assuranceNote: The check establishes that training-shaped code exists and no configuration artifact was found beside it. Config presence is not config sufficiency: whether what was recorded is enough to rerun the experiment is exactly the judgement reproducibility.no-unsubstantiated-claims asks a human to make.

rules.title: The resolved environment is recorded, by pins or by a lock artifact
rules.description: The environment a result came from is recorded, either by exact pins in the manifest or by a committed lock artifact beside a manifest that declares ranges. Ranges alone are not a record.
rules.rationale: An unpinned dependency means the environment that produced a result cannot be rebuilt, and in this domain a minor version change in a numerical library moves results rather than breaking builds — so the failure is a quiet difference in the numbers rather than an error.
rules.remediation: Either pin each declared dependency to an exact version, or commit the lock artifact your ecosystem produces beside the ranged manifest. A project consumed as a dependency should do the second.
rules.evidenceExpected: A requirements file with exact pins, or a manifest accompanied by a committed lockfile.
rules.$assuranceNote: The check reads what the manifest declares and reports the unpinned entries exactly. Pins in a manifest are not the environment the results came from: transitive versions, accelerator and BLAS builds, and operating-system differences are all outside what a manifest can fix.

rules.title: Reproducibility is not claimed without the configuration to support it
rules.description: A result must not be described as reproducible unless the recorded configuration is sufficient to obtain it again. Describing work as reproducible because a seed was set, or because the code is in version control, is this prohibition.
rules.rationale: A reproducibility claim is relied upon by everyone downstream who does not check it, which is everyone. The claim is cheap to make and expensive to falsify, so it must be earned rather than assumed.
rules.remediation: Either complete the configuration record until the result can be obtained again, or state plainly that the work is not currently reproducible and why.
rules.evidenceExpected: An attestation that someone reran an experiment from its recorded configuration and obtained the reported result, or an explicit statement that the work is not reproducible.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Verifying a reproducibility claim requires rerunning the training, which this tool does not do — executing the code under audit is outside its contract, and a rerun that agreed in a different environment would establish less than it appeared to.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible. The exemptible neighbour already exists and is honest: say the work is not reproducible. What cannot be waived is claiming it falsely, because an exception would sanction a statement that other people will rely on without checking.

rules.title: Every source of randomness is seeded and the seed is recorded
rules.description: Seeds are set explicitly for each source of randomness that affects the result — shuffling, initialisation, dropout, augmentation, and the split itself — and recorded alongside the result rather than only set in code.
rules.rationale: Setting a seed is the cheapest step toward reproducibility. It is a recommendation rather than a requirement because it neither guarantees determinism nor is always achievable, and because the requirement that actually matters is the configuration record it forms part of.
rules.remediation: Set and record a seed for each randomness source, and verify determinism by running twice rather than assuming it.
rules.evidenceExpected: Explicit seed values in the experiment configuration, and a determinism check showing two runs agree.
rules.$assuranceNote: The check establishes whether any seed-setting expression appears at all. Presence is not determinism: accelerator kernels, data-loader ordering, and unseeded library internals can each defeat a correctly set seed, and this check never claims a run is reproducible.

rules.title: Notebooks used to produce results carry no stale state
rules.description: A notebook whose outputs contributed to a reported result runs top to bottom, and the committed outputs correspond to that run rather than to an earlier session.
rules.rationale: A notebook executed out of order carries state no reader can reconstruct, and its committed outputs then document a computation that the code as written does not perform.
rules.remediation: Restart the kernel, run all cells, and commit the result — or strip outputs and move the result-producing path into a script.
rules.evidenceExpected: Notebooks whose execution counts ascend without gaps, or a scripted pipeline that produces the reported results outside a notebook.
rules.$assuranceNote: The check establishes two structural facts: that outputs are committed and that execution counts are not monotonic. Both are evidence of unrefreshed state rather than proof of irreproducibility, and a clean linear notebook is likewise not proof of reproducibility.
